task: prefill-commit dedup free/re-point vs in-flight overlapped decode step 1
source: CPU code analysis; native $N/python hash-identical to work/FreeToken-opt for scheduler.py, cache.py, prefill.py, hybrid_radix_cache.py, linear_state_pool.py, fi.py, graph.py, engine.py, layer_major.py x2 (hashcheck.sh)
invariant: Every GPU op lands on one of two streams that are chained at every hand-off, so they run in one total order: sched_k on self.stream (after wait @scheduler.py:241) -> B_k on engine stream (waits self.stream @249/253) -> drain_k on self.stream (waits engine @265) -> sched_{k+1}. Frees are CPU bookkeeping. A freed page or slot reaches a new owner only through an op enqueued after the drain, so it runs after every in-flight reader or writer.

evidence: scheduler.py:74 current stream = self.stream; drain (scheduler.py:266 -> 422 cache_req) runs outside engine_stream_ctx after scheduler.py:265 self.stream.wait_stream(engine.stream)

cache.py:428 dedup free -> lazy_free_region (scheduler.py:342, cache.py:604-619) appends freed pages to the BACK of free_slots, and _allocate takes from the FRONT (cache.py:639-640). Even an immediate reuse (via eviction) is a page_table write and KV writes enqueued after the drain

step 1 out_loc (scheduler.py:845) and FlashInfer indices (fi.py:300) are gathered on self.stream BEFORE the drain, so step 1 reads the request's own pages, which are intact. This matches l256 results.json: decode pos1 NLL exactly equal, first diff at pos2, identical across 3 runs

engine.py:1041 complete_one: at the drain cached_len=P+1, but the dedup range is [old_handle.cached_len, prefix_len) with prefix_len<=L<=P and L page-aligned (cache.py:403-405). Step 1's KV write page (position P) is never freed

side streams (moe offload_cache/slot_refill/weight_stream/complement) never reference page_table/kv_cache/linear_state_pool (grep moe/: none). Private libs launch on torch current stream (cuda_gdn.py:127.., cuda_kv.py:77, cuda_attention_gate.py:36)
layer-major path: job.step() on engine stream after wait (scheduler.py:248-250). Final-chunk commit follows the same launch-then-drain pattern. Abort drains via engine/layer_major.py:370-371

multi-request, prefix hits, cancellations: the prefix-hit node is locked before slot/page alloc (prefill.py:87 before 96/130). In-flight aborts are deferred to the drain (scheduler.py:600-607). The extra overlapped decode step of a finished request writes its freed pages/slot before any reuser in stream order

page_table is a device tensor (engine.py:430-434). The re-point is a D2D copy_ on self.stream (cache.py:435-437, generic 330-331) issued after scheduler.py:265, so it runs after step 1's indices snapshot (fi.py:300), graph input copy (graph.py:209) and FlashInfer plan copy into capture.indices (graph.py:211 -> fi.py:159), all enqueued earlier
insert clones the row slice (hybrid_radix_cache.py:101). lazy_free clones before the re-point (cache.py:611)
step 2 is prepared after the wait at scheduler.py:241, so it sees the canonical row. Pinned plan staging is guarded by last_event.synchronize (fi.py:155-157)

commit is zero-copy: the frozen ping-pong slot is donated (cache.py:423-425). The replacement comes from pool.alloc, which is LIFO (linear_state_pool.py:132,177), so a slot freed in the same drain can be reused at once. Its first GPU use (anchor copy cache.py:175 in _forward, COW restore scheduler.py:257) is on the engine stream after the in-flight batch
decode never touches ping-pong slots. The finish-donate of the live slot counts the in-flight extra step (cached_len after complete_one), so the snapshot matches the final GPU state

residual_note: Not a race: overlap step 1 reads the request's own prefix KV while steps 2+ read the canonical KV. Overlap and no-overlap runs therefore legitimately differ at step 1 when dedup fires, so their outputs are not a valid oracle for a stress test.
